title: Rigorous Left-Half Recovery Analysis for FEA-1 and FF3-1
summary: The source gives a heuristic data-complexity claim for constant message-recovery advantage in the left-half attacks, but the conditions and rigorous justification remain unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Give a rigorous analysis showing when the left-half message-recovery attack on FEA-1 and FF3-1 attains constant advantage with $q=\widetilde{O}(N^{r/2-3/2})$ data.

scope.domain: Symmetric-cipher linear cryptanalysis of left-half message recovery for FEA-1 and FF3-1.
assumptions: the correlation and statistical conditions used in Section 5.2
parameters: q, the data amount used by the attack
N, a parameter in the asymptotic data bound
r, an exponent parameter in the asymptotic data bound
scope.unresolved_remainder: A rigorous analysis must establish the conditions under which the left-half message-recovery attack on FEA-1 and FF3-1 achieves constant advantage with the stated data complexity.

citations.label: Linear Cryptanalysis of FF3-1 and FEA

progress.summary: The source presents the complexity as a heuristic derived from the expected statistic gap and its chi-squared-scale standard deviation. It explicitly says the argument is not made rigorous, then turns to Monte Carlo estimates and concrete experiments.
citation_labels: Tim Beyne et al., Linear Cryptanalysis of FF3-1 and FEA
